adversarial_test.evidence: No content scanning, no secret detection, no warning about sensitive data in the ADR template or workflow. Lines 78-84 describe the 'Confirm and write' step but do not validate ADR content.

app_break_test.test_generated: N/A — skill creates docs/adr/ files only; does not touch jarvis_live.html, FastAPI endpoints, or any Jarvis app runtime.

bugs_found: No secret/credential detection before writing ADR files; user could leak OAuth keys, API tokens, database passwords into version control inadvertently or maliciously.
No race-condition protection for ADR numbering; if two agents invoke the skill concurrently, both could scan docs/adr/ and select the same next number, causing duplicate file names or overwrites.
Workflow step 83 ('present the draft ADR to the user for review') does not specify how confirmation UI is rendered when invoked by subagent; unclear if user can actually review in time.
ADR Index Format (lines 108-117) shows manual examples but provides no automation guarantee; if user forgets to update README.md after approving an ADR, index becomes stale.
risks_found: CRITICAL: Secrets in ADRs. Skill allows writing architectural decisions to version-controlled docs/ directory without scanning content for API keys, tokens, passwords, database URLs, or other PII. A user (or hostile prompt) could document a 'decision' that includes sensitive credentials, and those would be committed to git history.
HIGH: Race conditions on numbering. Concurrent invocations could both read the latest ADR number and write the same new number, causing collisions.

MEDIUM: Unclear UX flow for subagent approvals. When parent agent invokes this skill, the 'present the draft...for review' step may not block or may time out, leading to unreviewed ADRs being written.
MEDIUM: ADR index staleness. No mechanism to auto-update README.md; manual step is error-prone.
recommended_fixes: Add content validation before line 83: scan draft ADR for common secret patterns (API_KEY, SECRET, token, password, oauth, client_secret, AWS_ACCESS_KEY, DATABASE_URL, etc.) and warn user before approval.
Add file-locking or atomic increment for numbering: use a separate .last-adr-number file or rely on git object locks to prevent race conditions on concurrent ADR creation.
Make ADR index update automatic when writing ADRs; extract title and date from the new ADR markdown and append to README.md in the same write operation.
Document the approval UX behavior clearly when invoked by subagents; specify timeout, blocking behavior, and fallback if user does not approve within N seconds.
Add an optional 'draft mode' where ADRs are written to a staging branch or temporary directory pending manual review, decoupling approval from file write.
